# 1 Clement Chapter 33 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_033_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 33

**33:1** What then shall we do, brothers? Shall we grow idle from good works and give up love? May the Master never allow this to befall us; but let us press forward with diligence and zeal to accomplish every good work.

**33:2** For the Creator and Master of all things himself rejoices in his own works.

**33:3** For by his all-powerful majesty he established the heavens, and by his unfathomable understanding he gave them their order; and the earth he separated from the water encircling it and set it firm upon the sure foundation of his own will; and the animals that walk upon it he called into being by his command; and having prepared beforehand the sea and the living creatures within it, he enclosed them by his power.

**33:4** Above all these, as the most excellent and incomparably greatest work of his understanding, he formed man with his holy and unblemished hands in the likeness of his own image.

**33:5** For God said thus: "Let us make man according to our image and our likeness. And God made man; male and female he made them."

**33:6** Having completed all these things, he praised and blessed them and said: "Be fruitful and multiply."

**33:7** Let us observe that all the righteous have been adorned with good works; so even the Lord himself, adorning himself with his works, rejoiced.

**33:8** Having therefore this pattern, let us without delay give heed to his will, and with all our strength let us perform the works of righteousness.

---

*LOGOS preserves the doxological sweep of the creation narrative and the careful chiasm of vv. 7-8.*
